videos.script: TLS protects one connection between two programs. Four other protocols use the same ideas at different places. {{title}} IPsec protects packets between two networks, below any application, which is how a branch office reaches head office. {{ipsec}} DNSSEC does not encrypt anything. It signs the answers of the DNS, so that a forged address is refused. {{dnssec}} SRTP protects the audio and video of a call, packet by packet, keyed by the same kind of exchange as TLS. {{srtp}} And S/MIME protects an e-mail itself, so the message stays signed and encrypted after it leaves the network, in every mailbox it reaches. {{smime}} Each answers the same question in its own place: what is protected, against whom, and who holds the key.
